definition: Acceleration that stays constant in magnitude and direction; the equations of motion apply only when the acceleration is uniform.
Acceleration that changes with time, shown by a curved velocity–time graph; the equations of motion do not apply, so use gradients and areas of graphs instead.

The area between a graph line and the horizontal axis, equal to the product of the two axis quantities added up: under a velocity–time graph it is the displacement, and under an acceleration–time graph the change in velocity.
The acceleration $g$ of a body acted on only by its weight; near Earth's surface it is $9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ downwards (data booklet), the same for every body.
